en.greeting: Hi! Today we travel to a moment in the future and describe it three ways: what you'll be doing then, what you'll have done by then, and how long you'll have been doing it. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Picture a moment in the future
steps.text: You already know will, going to and the present continuous for plans. Today we stand at one moment in the future and look around it.
steps.body:
Quick recap: **will / going to / am + -ing** for decisions, plans and arrangements, and **no will** after *when, before, as soon as* (B1).
New today, three ways to describe a future moment:
- **will be + -ing**: in the middle of it then (*sedang*)
- **will have + past participle**: already done by then (*sudah*)
- **will have been + -ing**: how long, up to then (*sudah … selama*)
Indonesian just adds *sedang* or *sudah* to *besok* or *nanti*; English needs the right future form.

pairs.en: by the time you get here

steps.title: Sari's future on one line
steps.text: Here's Sari's life on one line. She joined a startup in Jakarta in June 2022. Look at the three future moments.

timeline.title: Three ways to look at the future
timeline.caption: Tomorrow at 10 Sari is in the air → she'll be flying to Bali (in the middle). Her report is due on Friday and she'll send it before → by Friday she'll have finished it (done). She started in June 2022 → in June 2027 she'll have been working there for five years (how long).

marks.label: tomorrow 10:00 · in the air → she'll be flying
by Friday · report done → she'll have finished it
June 2027 · five years → she'll have been working there

steps.title: will be + -ing: in the middle
steps.text: First form: what will be **happening** at a moment in the future.
steps.body: **will be + -ing** = in progress at a future moment. It starts before and goes on after: *This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali.* Clues: **this time tomorrow, at 8 tonight, at 10 on Monday**. Compare: *At 8 I'll call you* (the call starts at 8) and *At 8 I'll be driving* (I'm in the middle of it). Trap: *Besok jam segini saya **sedang** terbang* → not 'I will fly' but **I'll be flying**. Polite phrase to remember: *Will you be using the car tonight?* = a soft way to ask about plans.

pairs.en: This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali.
pairs.id: Besok jam segini saya sedang terbang ke Bali.

steps.title: A call at 10?
steps.text: Pak Hasan wants to call you tomorrow morning.

question.prompt: Pak Hasan: 'Can I call you at 10 tomorrow morning?' You: 'Better not. My training session for new staff goes from 9 to 12, so at 10 I ___ it.'
question.explanation: At 10 the session is in the middle (it goes from 9 to 12), so use **will be + -ing**: **I'll be running it**. 'I'll run it' sounds like it starts at 10, and 'I'll have run it' means it's already finished by 10.

steps.title: will have + past participle: done
steps.text: Second form: what will be **finished** by a moment in the future.
steps.body: **will have + past participle** (the third form from the present perfect: *finished, written, left*) = done before a future moment: *By 2030 I'll have finished my degree.* **by** = paling lambat: *by Friday, by then, by the end of the year*. With a verb, **by the time** + present: *By the time you get here, the film will have started.* Trap: *Tahun 2030 saya **sudah** lulus* → not 'I already finish' or 'I have finished by 2030', but **I'll have finished**. And **by** isn't **until** (sampai, the whole time).

pairs.en: by the end of the year
By 2030 I'll have finished my degree.
pairs.id: Paling lambat tahun 2030 kuliah saya sudah selesai.

steps.title: Before the deadline
steps.text: The client is waiting for a contract.

question.prompt: The client needs the contract on Friday morning, and your manager looks worried. You: 'Don't worry. By Thursday evening I ___ it to them.'
question.explanation: Done before a future moment (Thursday evening) → **will have + past participle**: **I'll have sent it** (send → sent). 'already send' is word-for-word Indonesian (*sudah kirim*) with no future, and 'I've sent' is the present perfect: up to now, not up to Thursday.

steps.title: will have been + -ing: how long
steps.text: Third form: **how long** something will have been going on at a future moment.
steps.body: **will have been + -ing** = a duration up to a future moment. It's the present perfect continuous (*I've been working here for four years*) moved into the future: *By June I'll have been working here for five years.* You need **for + a period** and the moment (**by June, next year, when …**). Same form for every subject. Trap: *Juni nanti **sudah** lima tahun saya kerja di sini* → not 'In June I work here five years'. With **live, work, study**, *will have worked* is also fine; with state verbs (know, be) use only the simple: *I'll have known her for ten years*.

pairs.en: By June I'll have been working here for five years.
pairs.id: Juni nanti, sudah lima tahun saya bekerja di sini.

pairs.en: By the time the plane lands, we'll have been travelling for 20 hours.
pairs.id: Saat pesawatnya mendarat nanti, kami sudah 20 jam dalam perjalanan.

steps.title: Twenty years at school
steps.text: Bu Ani is a teacher in Bandung. Say what will be true next year.

question.prompt: Bu Ani started teaching at SMA 3 Bandung in June 2007. What will be true in June 2027? Arrange the words: Saat itu, dia sudah dua puluh tahun mengajar.
question.solution: She'll have been teaching for twenty years.
question.explanation: A duration up to a future moment (June 2027) → **will have been + -ing** + **for** + the period: *She'll have been teaching for twenty years.* **have** stays *have* even with *she*.

steps.title: Still no will after when
steps.text: One rule from the B1 lesson still works with the new forms.
steps.body: After **when, after, before, as soon as, until** and **by the time**, there's **no will**, not even *will have* or *will be*. Use the present simple, or the present perfect to stress 'finished'. The **will** goes in the other part: *I'll call you when I've finished* (or *when I finish*), not 'when I will have finished'. Indonesian trap: *Kabari saya kalau **sudah** selesai* has *sudah*, but English says **when you've finished**. A question is different: *When will you have finished?* is correct.

pairs.en: by the time you get here
I'll call you when I've finished.
pairs.id: Nanti saya telepon kalau sudah selesai.

steps.title: Dimas and the contract
steps.text: Dimas's boss sends him a quick message.

question.prompt: Dimas is checking a contract. His boss writes: 'Send it to the client as soon as you ___ it.'
question.explanation: After **as soon as** (like when, after, before, until, by the time) there's no will, even for the future. To stress 'finished', use the present perfect: **as soon as you've checked it** (*as soon as you check it* is also fine). 'will have checked' is the *kalau sudah* trap.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Future continuous & future perfect
artifact.intro: Picture a moment in the future: what's happening then, what's done by then, and how long it's been going on. No will after when, as soon as or by the time.
rows: will be + -ing
in progress at a future moment (sedang … nanti)
This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali.
won't be + -ing / Will you be + -ing?
negative / question (also a polite question about plans)
Will you be using the car tonight?
will have + past participle
done by a future moment (sudah … nanti)
By 2030 I'll have finished my degree.
won't have + past participle
not done yet at that moment (belum)
She won't have finished her shift by 9.
will have been + -ing + for …
how long, up to a future moment
By June I'll have been working here for five years.
by / by the time + present
deadline: paling lambat / saat … nanti
By the time we get there, the film will have started.
when / after / as soon as + present (perfect)
time clause: no will
I'll call you when I've finished.
tips: *sedang* + a future time → **will be + -ing**: 'This time tomorrow I will fly' → **I'll be flying**.
*sudah* + a future time → **will have + past participle**: 'By 2030 I already finish' → **I'll have finished**. **by** = deadline, **until** = the whole time.
No will in a time clause: 'when you will have finished' → **when you've finished**.

examples.en: Don't call me at 10. I'll be meeting a client.
examples.id: Jangan telepon saya jam 10. Saya sedang bertemu klien.

examples.en: Don't worry, I'll have sent the invoice by Friday.
examples.id: Tenang, paling lambat Jumat tagihannya sudah saya kirim.

examples.en: Next month Rina will have been learning English for three years.
examples.id: Bulan depan sudah tiga tahun Rina belajar bahasa Inggris.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more practice? This British Council page explains will be + -ing and will have + past participle, with two short tests.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita pergi ke satu saat di masa depan dan menggambarkannya dengan tiga cara: apa yang sedang kamu lakukan saat itu, apa yang sudah selesai saat itu, dan sudah berapa lama kamu melakukannya. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: Bayangkan satu saat di masa depan
steps.text: Kamu sudah kenal will, going to dan present continuous untuk rencana. Hari ini kita berdiri di satu saat di masa depan dan melihat sekelilingnya.
steps.body:
Pengingat singkat: **will / going to / am + -ing** untuk keputusan, rencana dan janji yang sudah diatur, dan **tanpa will** setelah *when, before, as soon as* (B1).
Yang baru hari ini, tiga cara menggambarkan satu saat di masa depan:
- **will be + -ing**: saat itu sedang di tengah kegiatan (*sedang*)
- **will have + past participle**: saat itu sudah selesai (*sudah*)
- **will have been + -ing**: sudah berapa lama, sampai saat itu (*sudah … selama*)
Bahasa Indonesia cukup menambah *sedang* atau *sudah* ke *besok* atau *nanti*; bahasa Inggris perlu bentuk masa depan yang tepat.

pairs.en: by the time you get here

steps.title: Masa depan Sari dalam satu garis
steps.text: Ini hidup Sari dalam satu garis. Dia mulai bekerja di sebuah startup di Jakarta pada Juni 2022. Perhatikan tiga saat di masa depan.

timeline.title: Tiga cara melihat masa depan
timeline.caption: Besok jam 10 Sari sedang di pesawat → she'll be flying to Bali (sedang di tengah kegiatan). Laporannya harus selesai hari Jumat dan dia akan mengirimnya sebelum itu → by Friday she'll have finished it (sudah selesai). Dia mulai bekerja Juni 2022 → in June 2027 she'll have been working there for five years (sudah berapa lama).

marks.label: besok 10:00 · di pesawat → she'll be flying
paling lambat Jumat · laporan selesai → she'll have finished it
Juni 2027 · lima tahun → she'll have been working there

steps.title: will be + -ing: sedang di tengah
steps.text: Bentuk pertama: apa yang **sedang terjadi** pada saat tertentu di masa depan.
steps.body: **will be + -ing** = sedang berlangsung pada saat tertentu di masa depan. Kegiatannya mulai sebelum saat itu dan masih berjalan sesudahnya: *This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali.* Petunjuknya: **this time tomorrow, at 8 tonight, at 10 on Monday**. Bandingkan: *At 8 I'll call you* (teleponnya mulai jam 8) dan *At 8 I'll be driving* (jam 8 saya sedang menyetir). Jebakan: *Besok jam segini saya **sedang** terbang* → bukan 'I will fly' tetapi **I'll be flying**. Frasa sopan untuk diingat: *Will you be using the car tonight?* = cara halus menanyakan rencana orang.

pairs.en: This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali.
pairs.id: Besok jam segini saya sedang terbang ke Bali.

steps.title: Telepon jam 10?
steps.text: Pak Hasan mau meneleponmu besok pagi.

question.prompt: Pak Hasan: 'Can I call you at 10 tomorrow morning?' Kamu: 'Better not. My training session for new staff goes from 9 to 12, so at 10 I ___ it.' (Pelatihan untuk karyawan baru berlangsung jam 9 sampai 12.)
question.explanation: Jam 10 pelatihannya sedang berjalan (dari jam 9 sampai 12), jadi pakai **will be + -ing**: **I'll be running it**. 'I'll run it' terdengar seperti baru mulai jam 10, dan 'I'll have run it' berarti sudah selesai sebelum jam 10.

steps.title: will have + past participle: sudah selesai
steps.text: Bentuk kedua: apa yang **sudah selesai** pada saat tertentu di masa depan.
steps.body: **will have + past participle** (bentuk ketiga dari present perfect: *finished, written, left*) = sudah selesai sebelum saat tertentu di masa depan: *By 2030 I'll have finished my degree.* **by** = paling lambat: *by Friday, by then, by the end of the year*. Dengan kata kerja, **by the time** + present: *By the time you get here, the film will have started.* Jebakan: *Tahun 2030 saya **sudah** lulus* → bukan 'I already finish' atau 'I have finished by 2030', tetapi **I'll have finished**. Dan **by** tidak sama dengan **until** (sampai, terus-menerus).

pairs.en: by the end of the year
By 2030 I'll have finished my degree.
pairs.id: Paling lambat tahun 2030 kuliah saya sudah selesai.

steps.title: Sebelum tenggat
steps.text: Klien sedang menunggu kontrak.

question.prompt: Klien butuh kontraknya hari Jumat pagi, dan manajermu terlihat khawatir. Kamu: 'Don't worry. By Thursday evening I ___ it to them.'
question.explanation: Sudah selesai sebelum saat tertentu di masa depan (Kamis malam) → **will have + past participle**: **I'll have sent it** (send → sent). 'already send' adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari *sudah kirim* tanpa bentuk masa depan, dan 'I've sent' adalah present perfect: sampai sekarang, bukan sampai hari Kamis.

steps.title: will have been + -ing: berapa lama
steps.text: Bentuk ketiga: **sudah berapa lama** sebuah kegiatan berjalan pada saat tertentu di masa depan.
steps.body: **will have been + -ing** = lamanya kegiatan sampai saat tertentu di masa depan. Ini present perfect continuous (*I've been working here for four years*) yang dipindah ke masa depan: *By June I'll have been working here for five years.* Kamu perlu **for + lamanya** dan saatnya (**by June, next year, when …**). Bentuknya sama untuk semua subjek. Jebakan: *Juni nanti **sudah** lima tahun saya kerja di sini* → bukan 'In June I work here five years'. Dengan **live, work, study**, *will have worked* juga benar; dengan kata kerja keadaan (know, be) pakai bentuk simple saja: *I'll have known her for ten years*.

pairs.en: By June I'll have been working here for five years.
pairs.id: Juni nanti, sudah lima tahun saya bekerja di sini.

pairs.en: By the time the plane lands, we'll have been travelling for 20 hours.
pairs.id: Saat pesawatnya mendarat nanti, kami sudah 20 jam dalam perjalanan.

steps.title: Dua puluh tahun mengajar
steps.text: Bu Ani guru di Bandung. Katakan apa yang benar tahun depan.

question.prompt: Bu Ani mulai mengajar di SMA 3 Bandung pada Juni 2007. Apa yang benar pada Juni 2027? Susun kata-katanya: Saat itu, dia sudah dua puluh tahun mengajar.
question.solution: She'll have been teaching for twenty years.
question.explanation: Lamanya sampai saat tertentu di masa depan (Juni 2027) → **will have been + -ing** + **for** + lamanya: *She'll have been teaching for twenty years.* **have** tetap *have* walaupun subjeknya *she*.

steps.title: Tetap tanpa will setelah when
steps.text: Satu aturan dari pelajaran B1 tetap berlaku untuk bentuk-bentuk baru ini.
steps.body: Setelah **when, after, before, as soon as, until** dan **by the time**, **tidak ada will**, termasuk *will have* atau *will be*. Pakai present simple, atau present perfect untuk menekankan 'sudah selesai'. **will** ditaruh di bagian yang lain: *I'll call you when I've finished* (atau *when I finish*), bukan 'when I will have finished'. Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *Kabari saya kalau **sudah** selesai* punya *sudah*, tapi bahasa Inggris bilang **when you've finished**. Pertanyaan berbeda: *When will you have finished?* benar.

pairs.en: by the time you get here
I'll call you when I've finished.
pairs.id: Nanti saya telepon kalau sudah selesai.

steps.title: Dimas dan kontraknya
steps.text: Atasan Dimas mengirim pesan singkat.

question.prompt: Dimas sedang memeriksa kontrak. Atasannya menulis: 'Send it to the client as soon as you ___ it.'
question.explanation: Setelah **as soon as** (seperti when, after, before, until, by the time) tidak ada will, walaupun membicarakan masa depan. Untuk menekankan 'sudah selesai', pakai present perfect: **as soon as you've checked it** (*as soon as you check it* juga benar). 'will have checked' adalah jebakan *kalau sudah*.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Future continuous & future perfect
artifact.intro: Bayangkan satu saat di masa depan: apa yang sedang terjadi saat itu, apa yang sudah selesai, dan sudah berapa lama kegiatannya berjalan. Tanpa will setelah when, as soon as atau by the time.
rows: will be + -ing
sedang berlangsung pada saat tertentu di masa depan (sedang … nanti)
This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Bali.
won't be + -ing / Will you be + -ing?
negatif / pertanyaan (juga pertanyaan sopan tentang rencana)
Will you be using the car tonight?
will have + past participle
sudah selesai pada saat tertentu di masa depan (sudah … nanti)
By 2030 I'll have finished my degree.
won't have + past participle
saat itu belum selesai
She won't have finished her shift by 9.
will have been + -ing + for …
sudah berapa lama, sampai saat tertentu di masa depan
By June I'll have been working here for five years.
by / by the time + present
tenggat: paling lambat / saat … nanti
By the time we get there, the film will have started.
when / after / as soon as + present (perfect)
time clause: tanpa will
I'll call you when I've finished.
tips: *sedang* + waktu masa depan → **will be + -ing**: 'This time tomorrow I will fly' → **I'll be flying**.
*sudah* + waktu masa depan → **will have + past participle**: 'By 2030 I already finish' → **I'll have finished**. **by** = tenggat, **until** = terus sampai saat itu.
Tanpa will di time clause: 'when you will have finished' → **when you've finished**.

examples.en: Don't worry, I'll have sent the invoice by Friday.
examples.id: Tenang, paling lambat Jumat tagihannya sudah saya kirim.

examples.en: Next month Rina will have been learning English for three years.
examples.id: Bulan depan sudah tiga tahun Rina belajar bahasa Inggris.

steps.title: Belajar lebih lanjut
steps.text: Mau latihan lagi? Halaman British Council ini menjelaskan will be + -ing dan will have + past participle, dengan dua tes singkat.
